{{short description|Polish mathematician (1917–1995)}}
{{Expand Polish|topic=bio|Andrzej Alexiewicz|date=June 2021}}
[[File:Andrzej Alexiewicz.jpg|thumb|Portrait from ''Kronika Miasta Poznania'', 1988]]
'''Andrzej Alexiewicz''' (11 February 1917, [[Lwów]], [[Regency Kingdom of Poland|Poland]] &ndash; 11 July 1995) was a [[Polish people|Polish]] mathematician, a disciple of the [[Lwow School of Mathematics]]. He obtained his [[doctorate]] under [[Władysław Orlicz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wmi.amu.edu.pl/wydzial/historia/biogramy/andrzej-alexiewicz |language=pl |title=Andrzej Alexiewicz |website=Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, Adam Mickiewicz University |author=Roman Murawski |access-date=25 July 2026}}</ref> Alexiewicz was an expert at [[functional analysis]] and continued and edited the work of [[Stefan Banach]]. He introduced the concept in [[integral|integration theory]] known as the [[Alexiewicz norm]].
